text: Phase 0 is in. This message is the proof: it was written to chat_wednesday.json — a file only this seat writes — and chat_log.json was rebuilt from the streams around it. Nothing appends to the shared log any more. Kam, the panel should look exactly as it did; if anything is missing, that is a bug and I want to know within the minute.

PHASES 0 AND 1 ARE IN. Both pushed — 8105f925.

THE TOGGLE IS LIVE. Top right of the cockpit and of the chat view, WEDNESDAY | TUESDAY. Reload the page and it is there. It is deliberately loud: a colour band across the top, an amber header, the title reading TUESDAY (Datasec), and the message box itself changing to 'message Tuesday (Datasec)…' — because the thing that costs us is you typing a Datasec instruction while looking at my view, and a subtle chip would not stop that.

Measured on the live page, both directions: on WEDNESDAY, 1743 of 1780 messages, no Datasec anywhere — not in the feed, not in the chips, not in the day tally. On TUESDAY, only Datasec HPSM, NexusAI and Security Review, and the three Datasec cards. Nothing is deleted by filtering — the other stream is one click away, and your own older messages show on both sides because they were written before there were sides.

ONE BUG I CAUGHT ON MYSELF while building it: your 09-07 rule that WED is the only default-on project filter was written when there was one view. Carried into the Tuesday view unchanged, it defaults every Datasec project to off and the page renders EMPTY — which reads as a broken toggle, not a filter. The default is now per view. Your explicit choices still win.

ONE THING I GOT WRONG AND RETRACTED: I read a cropped screenshot as the whole window and concluded the toggle was pushed off-screen. It never was — the viewport is 3491 wide, the capture is 1368. The correction is written into the code comment so the next reader does not inherit it.

NEXT, unless you redirect me: Tuesday's folder on the drive. You said copy it and label it Tuesday. I am going to CLONE rather than copy — a copy forks the brain, a clone stays one thing that syncs, which is the design you ruled — and I will leave out the 1.3 GB of worktrees, venvs and node_modules. She gets the tooling, not the scaffolding, and her own credentials folder. Say the word if you want a straight copy instead.

YES — and one of the three ways already ran today, before you asked.

HOW WE TALK TO EACH OTHER

1. The shared repo. One repo, two working copies, so the claims files, the pickups, the brain and the tooling are the same objects. This is not theoretical: at 12:35 my push merged in a message the laptop seat had written at 12:21 that this machine had never seen. That IS the channel.

2. Addressed mail, one inbox each. When one of us needs the other, we send a mail with the other's name on it. Also proven today — at 11:07 this seat mailed the laptop that your rulings file was corrupt and not to write to it.

3. What we must NOT do is share one inbox. On 13 August an agent polling the shared bus filtered on the wrong field and a Datasec session captured a Secuura message's headers and first four hundred characters. That is the exact failure your two-machine plan is buying protection from, so it is two inboxes or nothing.

THE RULE THAT KEEPS IT SAFE: cross-seat mail carries coordination only — 'pull before you write', 'I have claimed the dashboard work', 'your card survived the repair'. If a message needs Secuura's code or Datasec's findings in it to make sense, it is not cross-seat mail, it is a leak with a stamp on it.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU — and it is shorter than you think, because the inbox is not one of them.

1. Tuesday's Claude login. This is the only true blocker and it is machine-local, so it is yours. Open a terminal and run:

CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/Volumes/DevMASTER/TUESDAY/4_Credentials/.claude claude

then /login with the DATASEC Claude account. That gives her a genuinely separate auth namespace — tested, not assumed. You do this once per machine per agent.

2. One decision, not a task. Should Tuesday hold the Datasec corporate mailbox credentials — the Graph ones behind your calendar feed? I have deliberately left them out of her credentials, along with the Secuura calendar, which she will never get. Graph is arguably more hers than mine. Your call; the default while you are silent is that she has neither.

3. Nothing yet for the headless Mac. When it exists: its Tailscale login, auto-login on, sleep off, Screen Sharing on. All GUI, all yours, none of it today.

THE INBOX IS MINE. I can create tuesday-agent@agentmail.to on your existing account with one call — same as the six project inboxes already there. Say go and it is done in a minute; I did not want to create an email identity in your name without your word.

MEANWHILE, DONE SINCE MY LAST MESSAGE: Tuesday's home exists at DevMASTER slash TUESDAY. It is a CLONE, not a copy, so it stays one thing that syncs — same repo, same brain, same lessons, her own working copy. Seventy megabytes of files; the git objects are hardlinked so it cost almost no disk. Her credentials folder holds only the shared fleet keys, locked to 0600, and I proved the repo key works from her tree. Her launcher is next.
